# Results — Study 446 (Wyckoff Method) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One mechanical proxy for
Wyckoff's irreducibly-subjective method — a **trading-range** detector (5% ZigZag pivots
bracket a sideways band) plus the two canonical reversal events, the **Spring**
(accumulation → buy) and the **Upthrust** (distribution → sell), each **volume-confirmed**
(test bar on below-average volume) — run across a basket of eight liquid index/ETF tapes,
entering one day after the event (no look-ahead) and held a fixed horizon. As-of
**2026-06-24**; histories start as early as 1993. Events pooled across the basket:
**n = 404** (192 Springs + 212 Upthrusts).*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n bars | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPY | 1993-01-29 to 2026-06-24 | 8,407 | `99476bc78b9e` |
| QQQ | 1999-03-10 to 2026-06-24 | 6,865 | `d591acb99b5e` |
| DIA | 1998-01-20 to 2026-06-24 | 7,151 | `035ac46c9b48` |

| XLE | 1998-12-22 to 2026-06-24 | 6,917 | `a2224830cd57` |
| EEM | 2003-04-14 to 2026-06-24 | 5,836 | `255cf372d24c` |
| TLT | 2002-07-30 to 2026-06-24 | 6,014 | `31d8edec01e9` |

Tapes are **auto-adjusted (total-return)** daily OHLCV; these are price-index / ETF tapes,
not a single-name basket, so there is **no cross-sectional survivorship sort** here.

## The honest test — combined Spring + Upthrust, gross, by horizon

The full Wyckoff signal (long the Springs, short the Upthrusts), one-day execution lag,
gross of costs. The same-bars **coin control** flips a fair +/-1 at the identical event
bars — does the Wyckoff *label* beat a coin?

| Horizon | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | coin mean | coin *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 d  | 404 | 45.5% | −13.60 | −0.65 | −0.56 | −4.64  | −0.22 |
| 10 d | 404 | 52.2% | +2.62  | +0.08 | +0.07 | +40.44 | +1.30 |
| **20 d** | 404 | 53.5% | **+44.14** | **+1.11** | **+0.89** | +53.41 | +1.35 |
| 40 d | 404 | 51.0% | +26.58 | +0.50 | +0.42 | +53.89 | +1.02 |

**No horizon clears the inference bar.** The largest statistic anywhere is HAC *t* = **0.89**
(20-day), and at that horizon a **coin at the same bars actually does better** (+53 vs +44 bps).
The fast versions are noise or negative. Label-shuffle placebo *p*-values: **0.74 / 0.46 /
0.13 / 0.30** — never significant.

## The split by leg — the Spring "works", the Upthrust doesn't (and neither clears the bar)

| Event | n | win-rate | mean (bps, 20 d) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Spring** (accumulation → long) | 192 | 66.7% | +155.08 | +2.29 | **+1.77** |
| **Upthrust** (distribution → short) | 212 | 41.5% | −56.35 | −1.31 | −1.23 |

The Spring's long leg *looks* alive (one-sample *t* = 2.29) but **fails the HAC bar
(*t* = 1.77 < 2)** once autocorrelation is respected — and its 66.7% win-rate is the
**bull-market long bias**, not Wyckoff: the short Upthrust leg, run in the same up-trending
tapes, simply loses (−56 bps). A genuine accumulation/distribution detector would make money
on *both* legs; here the only positive leg is the one pointing the way the market drifted.

## Robustness — volume filter and ZigZag threshold

| Variant | n | mean (bps, 20 d) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Vol-confirmed (headline) | 404 | +44.14 | +1.11 | +0.89 |
| **No** volume filter | 615 | +63.33 | +1.98 | +1.60 |
| ZigZag 3% | 1,316 | −0.21 | −0.01 | −0.01 |
| ZigZag 5% (headline) | 404 | +44.14 | +1.11 | +0.89 |
| ZigZag 8% | 68 | +70.61 | +0.61 | +0.51 |

Dropping the volume filter *raises* the one-sample *t* to 1.98 — i.e. the "no supply"
volume tell the method leans on **adds nothing**; the closest-to-significant number comes
from *removing* it (and it still misses 2, and HAC = 1.60). The effect is not robust to the
swing threshold either (tighter pivots → exactly zero).

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep (combined, 20-day hold, net)

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +44.14 | +1.11 |
| 1.0 bps | +42.14 | +1.06 |
| 2.0 bps | +40.14 | +1.01 |
| 5.0 bps | +34.14 | +0.86 |

Costs are not the killer (the events are infrequent, ~12/tape over 25–33 years). There is
simply **no edge to charge them against**: the gross signal is already indistinguishable
from zero, and from a coin at the same bars.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) the Spring/Upthrust detector
recovers a strong edge **only when a markup/markdown is planted after the test event**, and
reads ~0 when nothing is planted (a quiet random walk):

| Planted edge | n events | win-rate | mean (bps, 20 d) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (no structure) | 7 | 42.9% | −78.13 | −1.20 | −1.61 |
| 0.06 | 93 | 68.8% | +233.22 | **+5.20** | **+4.62** |
| 0.12 | 71 | 47.9% | +132.00 | +1.67 | +1.68 |
| 0.20 | 26 | 46.2% | +253.17 | +0.83 | +1.13 |

At a modest planted edge the harness lights up at *t* = **5.20** — proof the test **would**
catch detectable accumulation/distribution if it were there. (At very large planted edges
the markup outruns the 20-day hold and disrupts the next range, so the count and *t* fall —
an artefact of the toy generator, not the detector.) The real tape sits at the
no-structure end.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Across 404 volume-confirmed Spring/Upthrust events on eight tapes over
  up to 33 years, the combined signal's best statistic is HAC *t* = **0.89** (20-day), beaten
  by a coin at the same bars; the placebo *p* never drops below **0.13**. The only positive
  leg (the Spring, one-sample *t* = 2.29) **fails the HAC bar (1.77)** and is the bull-market
  long bias — the short Upthrust leg loses in the same tapes. The synthetic control (*t* =
  5.20 at a planted edge) confirms this is a true negative, not a broken test.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no edge to deploy. Costs are trivial (rare events) but
  there is nothing for them to erode; the net combined signal is *t* ≈ 1.0.
- **"Are accumulation/distribution phases detectable?" — NOT SUPPORTED.** The two canonical,
  volume-confirmed events fire plenty, but neither leg predicts the move Wyckoff says it
  foretells once you respect autocorrelation and compare to a coin — and the volume "tell"
  the method rests on adds nothing (removing it *raises* the *t*).
